subject: feat(storage): Add HDFS support via opendal services-hdfs-native (#3111)
body:
* feat(storage): Add HDFS support via opendal services-hdfs-native

Adds an opendal-hdfs-native cargo feature plus OpenDalStorageFactory::Hdfs
and OpenDalStorage::Hdfs variants in iceberg-storage-opendal, using
OpenDAL's services-hdfs-native (pure-Rust HDFS RPC, no JNI/libhdfs).

The NameNode for a path resolves as: the hdfs.name-node property when set
(comma-separated endpoints enable HA failover), otherwise the path
authority. hadoop.-prefixed properties are forwarded to the HDFS client
configuration, overriding values loaded from $HADOOP_CONF_DIR. Operators
are cached per effective NameNode since each holds live RPC connections.

Revives and updates PR #2441 (by @jordepic) against the current storage
layer and opendal 0.58, where name_node became mandatory and the comma
list is the HA mechanism.

Closes #2440

Co-authored-by: Jordan Epstein <jordepic@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: address review — Properties derive for HdfsConfig, drop HDFS CI special-casing

- HdfsConfig is now pub(crate) and parsed via #[derive(Properties)]
  (key/prefix attributes) instead of hand-written TryFrom + TypedBuilder.
- HDFS integration tests are no longer #[ignore]d and the dedicated CI
  step is gone; they run under the default nextest invocation since
  make docker-up already starts the fixture and the Tests job is
  Linux-only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: reject non-hierarchical hdfs URLs; key delete_stream batches by effective NameNode

- Url::parse accepts non-hierarchical forms like `hdfs:x`; the byte-7
  slice then panicked. Require the literal `hdfs://` prefix instead.
- batch_key_for_path grouped by URL host only, so NameNodes differing
  by port shared one deleter; key by the effective NameNode (configured
  hdfs.name-node, else authority incl. port), matching the operator cache.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(storage): rename hdfs module to hdfs_native, drop unused HdfsConfig

Per review: the opendal module, its functions and the storage/factory
variants are now hdfs_native-prefixed (leaving room for a libhdfs-backed
variant, see #1130), and the never-consumed HdfsConfig struct is removed
from the core crate — config/hdfs.rs keeps only the property constants
that iceberg-storage-opendal uses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: retrigger after setup-python manifest timeout on macos runner

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): address review — cache newtype, build outside lock, single NameNode rule, env-gated HDFS tests

- HdfsNativeOperatorCache newtype keeps the cache representation out of
  the public API.
- Operators are built outside the cache lock (the build reads Hadoop XML
  synchronously); a racing first caller's duplicate is dropped unopened.
- hdfs_native_effective_name_node is the single source of the
  configured-else-authority rule for both create_operator and the
  delete_stream batch key; unresolvable paths key on themselves.
- hdfs.name-node is trimmed and an empty value is treated as unset, so it
  no longer shadows the path-authority fallback.
- HDFS integration tests self-skip unless ICEBERG_TEST_HDFS_ENDPOINT is
  set (as the HF tests do) and the compose services sit behind the hdfs
  profile; the Linux CI job opts in via env.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(deps): bump rustls to 0.23.45 (RUSTSEC-2026-0285)

Inherited from main (tracked in #3222); same bump as #3165.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(storage): pin IPv6 authority handling in HDFS path parsing

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): resolve the HDFS NameNode in relativize_path too

An authority-less path now errors in relativize_path exactly as in create_operator unless hdfs.name-node is set, so the two cannot disagree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(storage): state the cost of the synchronous HDFS operator build

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(storage): describe the HDFS operator cache lifecycle

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): normalize each entry of the hdfs.name-node list

A space after a comma was passed through to opendal unchanged, which silently broke failover to that NameNode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(storage): accept PyIceberg's hdfs.host/hdfs.port for authority-less HDFS paths

They map to Hadoop's fs.defaultFS and apply only when the path has no authority, as in PyIceberg; hdfs.name-node stays the explicit override.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): require a port in every hdfs.name-node entry

An entry without a port can only fail at the first I/O as 'invalid socket address'; reject it at build time with the property and entry named. Bare host:port stays accepted, as in Hadoop and opendal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(storage): state the runtime binding of cached HDFS operators

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(storage): cover two-NameNode delete_stream batches and first-insert-wins caching

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(utils): name the HDFS port constant like its siblings

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): rebuild cached HDFS operators once their runtime is gone

Each cache entry parks a sentinel task on the runtime that built the operator and keeps a Weak to a token the task owns. When that runtime shuts down the token dies, the entry reads as stale and the operator is rebuilt on the current runtime instead of hdfs-native panicking on the dead one. Sentinels are aborted when entries drop.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): resolve HDFS NameNodes like Hadoop does

An authority with a port is used as is; hdfs.name-node serves logical nameservice authorities and authority-less paths, which otherwise fall back to fs.defaultFS. Portless strings from any source are logical names that only hdfs.name-node resolves, reported at resolution instead of at the first I/O.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(storage): keep the HDFS operator cache out of the public API

OpenDalStorage::HdfsNative now wraps one opaque HdfsNativeStorage with crate-private fields, built only by the factories. The serialized form keeps its nesting; the io-timeout propagation test now covers the HDFS factory too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(storage): build HDFS operators on a blocking thread

The build reads the Hadoop XML config synchronously; create_operator is now async and offloads it with spawn_blocking, outside the cache lock as before. The builder itself stays sync and runtime-free.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: run the HDFS integration tests in their own job

The default suite no longer pulls the Hadoop image or waits on the HDFS health checks; a dedicated required job starts only the two HDFS containers and runs the HDFS test binary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): stop dropping HDFS properties silently

PyIceberg's hdfs.user and hdfs.kerberos_ticket log a warning instead of vanishing (opendal's config has no user field), hdfs.port is validated whether or not a host is set and warns when it has no host to apply to, and a bare hadoop. key is rejected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(storage): derive the second NameNode spelling from the endpoint host

Resolving the host to its IPv4 address gives any hostname endpoint a second batch key; an IP-literal endpoint skips the test explicitly instead of passing as a no-op.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: record tracing as a dependency of iceberg-storage-opendal in Cargo.lock

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): report a missing tokio runtime instead of panicking in HDFS create_operator

The runtime handle is resolved up front and passed into the cache, so the sentinel is no longer optional and the unreachable no-runtime branch is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): normalize every HDFS NameNode spelling to hdfs://host:port

One parser classifies configured entries, path authorities and fs.defaultFS: other schemes, logical names, port 0, userinfo, paths and unbracketed IPv6 are rejected, and bare and prefixed spellings share one cache key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(storage): declare HDFS nameservices with hdfs.name-node.<nameservice>

The key expands to Hadoop's dfs.ha.namenodes and dfs.namenode.rpc-address keys in the forwarded options and the resolver reads them back, so nameservices declared through hadoop.* work the same way. Plain hdfs.name-node stays the documented single-cluster default; an undeclared name without it is a pointed error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): require a declaration for every logical HDFS nameservice

Plain hdfs.name-node serves authority-less paths only; an undeclared logical authority is an error naming the key to set instead of a guess that could reach the wrong cluster.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): reject userinfo and port 0 in HDFS path authorities

Userinfo was silently dropped and port 0 was misread as a logical nameservice; both are DataInvalid now, and the userinfo message names the host only so a password never reaches a log.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): validate the NameNode composed from hdfs.host and hdfs.port

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(storage): use an authority-less path in the cross-runtime HDFS test

A logical authority now requires a declaration, so the test must take the plain-key route.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(storage): tighten the HDFS tests after review

Drop three redundant unit tests, assert the warnings and the password redaction directly, make the serde round trip populate the cache first, check which error each negative case produces, cover the plain key and hdfs.host serving authority-less paths against the fixture, and name the declared-nameservice test for what it does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): mask userinfo in HDFS errors that echo a path or NameNode

A path that failed to parse, or had another scheme, was echoed whole, so
`hdfs://user:pw@nn:bad/x` put the password in the error. The NameNode
config errors (`hdfs.name-node`, `hdfs.name-node.<nameservice>`,
`hdfs.host`/`hdfs.port`, `fs.defaultFS`) echoed their values the same way.

Every `Invalid hdfs path` error now goes through one helper, and the config
errors use the same masking: everything between the scheme and the last
`@` becomes `***`, so a password holding a raw `/`, `?`, `#` or `://` is
covered too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): recover a poisoned HDFS operator cache lock

A panic elsewhere while the cache lock was held turned every later HDFS
call into a permanent `Unexpected` error. Writes only ever replace whole
entries, so the map stays consistent: both lock sites now recover the
guard with `PoisonError::into_inner`, and `get`/`insert` are infallible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(storage): flush the fake NameNode before sampling dials

The runtime test sampled its dial counter before the listener thread had
necessarily counted every dial from the first runtime. It now drops that
runtime and waits for the listener to close a marker connection; accepts
are served in order, so every earlier dial is counted first. A failed
accept no longer stops the listener.

The runtime-shutdown unit test also asserts that the rebuilt operator is
a new instance, not the stale one with a fresh sentinel.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(storage): state where portless HDFS authorities differ from Hadoop

Hadoop resolves a portless authority from hdfs-site.xml, else dials port
8020. Here it must be declared with `hdfs.name-node.<nameservice>`,
because opendal builds the client as `hdfs://nameservice` and never hands
hdfs-native the authority. The `HDFS_NAME_NODE` and resolver docs no
longer claim Hadoop parity, the error says to add a port or declare the
nameservice, and the README notes the limitation in its own note.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(storage): rename the HDFS config module to hdfs_native

Matches its siblings, which are named after their storage feature
(azdls, gcs, hf, oss, s3). The module is private and re-exported, so the
public iceberg::io::HDFS_* paths are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(storage): move the HDFS tests out of lib.rs into hdfs_native

The serde round-trip and relativize_path tests now live next to the code
they cover, with the module's test_hdfs_native_ prefix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(storage): read HDFS properties through #[derive(Properties)]

hdfs.name-node, the hdfs.name-node.<nameservice> and hadoop. prefixes,
hdfs.host and hdfs.port are declared in one struct parsed by the
Properties macro instead of being looked up by hand. Host and port stay
trimmed strings so a blank value still counts as unset, as in PyIceberg.
Validation, warnings and error messages are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: run the HDFS tests in the default suite like the other fixtures

The HDFS fixture joins the shared bridge network with published ports
instead of using host networking behind a compose profile, so make
docker-up starts it on every platform: the DataNode advertises 127.0.0.1
and the tests set dfs.client.use.datanode.hostname. The tests no longer
skip without ICEBERG_TEST_HDFS_ENDPOINT, and the dedicated Tests (hdfs)
job is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): build HDFS clients in a crate-owned runtime

An hdfs-native client spawns its NameNode connections on the runtime
current when it is built and panics once that runtime is dropped. The
cache used to detect that with a sentinel task per entry, which needed
Handle::try_current, and the build ran under spawn_blocking, which made
create_operator async for every backend. Clients are now built inside a
crate-owned runtime started on first use, so a cached operator works
from any caller's runtime: the sentinel, Handle::try_current and
spawn_blocking are gone, and create_operator is sync again as on main.
The Hadoop XML read (~0.1 ms) runs inline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(storage): type HDFS path authorities and validate declarations at parse

hdfs_native_parse_path returns an HdfsNativeAuthority (NameNode,
Nameservice, Default), so the resolver matches on it instead of
re-parsing the authority to learn whether it has a port. Every HA
nameservice declaration, from hdfs.name-node.<nameservice> or passed
through as hadoop.dfs.ha.namenodes.*, and the fs.defaultFS that serves
authority-less paths are now validated when the config is parsed, so a
broken one fails the first call rather than only the paths that use it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(storage): drop index slicing and combinator chains in the HDFS backend

The nameservice lookup is a for loop with let-else, and the userinfo
masking and the relative-path extraction use split_once/rsplit_once
instead of slicing at computed indices. A test pins that doubled slashes
after the authority are still trimmed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): attach the hdfs.port parse error as the source

The parse error was interpolated into the message; it is now attached
as the error's source, which iceberg prints after the message.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): share one HDFS client across host name spellings

host_str keeps the host's case for hdfs:// URLs, so hdfs://NN1:8020 and
hdfs://nn1:8020 cached two clients for one NameNode. Endpoint hosts are
now lowercased by one helper used by the config normalizer and the path
parser, as Hadoop's FileSystem cache key does; nameservice names stay
case-sensitive like the Hadoop keys that declare them. The cache's doc
states that it is unbounded by design.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(storage): note the upstream gap behind the HDFS client runtime

opendal's hdfs-native service does not expose hdfs-native's
ClientBuilder::with_io_runtime (Kimahriman/hdfs-native#255); a TODO at
the crate-owned runtime records that a runtime could be passed in once
it does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(storage): make the HDFS HA test fail over for real

The declared-nameservice test listed the single-node fixture twice,
which drove opendal's list path but never needed a failover. Its first
NameNode is now a local port nothing listens on, so every call has to
fail over through opendal's synthetic nameservice; an opendal change
that kept only the first entry of the list would fail it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: retrigger CI

Docker Hub rate-limited the previous run's image pulls, so the default test job never started its fixtures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: retrigger CI

The previous run hit Docker Hub's unauthenticated pull rate limit again before any test ran.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(storage): document how to enable and configure the HDFS backend

The iceberg-storage-opendal README gains an HDFS section: enabling the
opendal-hdfs-native feature, the factory, the hdfs.* and hadoop.*
properties, the Hadoop config, user and Kerberos it reads, and the
portless-authority limitation. The experimental-backends note now points
to it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(storage): drop the HDFS README section and link follow-up issues

Configuration docs for every backend are tracked in #3510; the README
keeps the one-line note on the portless-authority limitation. The TODO on
the crate-owned HDFS runtime now points at #3509.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(expr): widen promoted partition values and bounds to prevent false pruning (#3483)
body:
* fix(expr): widen promoted partition values before comparison

A partition column promoted int->long (or float->double) keeps its
originally-written values in manifests produced before the promotion.
The entry partition tuple is decoded under the manifest's own narrower
type, while the scan predicate is bound to the current wider type.
`Datum::partial_cmp`/`PartialEq` require matching types, so the
`ExpressionEvaluator` compared e.g. an int partition value against a
long predicate literal, got no ordering, and silently pruned the data
file, dropping matching rows from filtered scans.

The manifest-list `ManifestEvaluator` is unaffected: it decodes
`FieldSummary` bounds with `Datum::try_from_bytes`, which already widens
a 4-byte int bound to long. Mirror that on the entry path by widening
the partition value to the reference's type before comparing. Decimals
already compare across precisions, so only int->long and float->double
need widening.

Co-authored-by: Isaac <no-reply@databricks.com>

* fix(expr): widen promoted column bounds in metrics pruning

Companion to the partition-tuple widening: InclusiveMetricsEvaluator
compares a data file's column bounds against the scan predicate, but
those bounds are decoded under the manifest's embedded (narrower) schema
while the predicate is bound to the current (wider) type. For an int
column promoted to long (or float to double), the inequality and IN
checks compared mismatched types, got no ordering, and discarded files
that could match, dropping rows; the eq check failed open and merely
skipped valid pruning.

Widen each stored bound to the reference's type before comparing, via
the same `Datum::promote_to` helper, in the inequality, eq, and IN paths.

* fix(scan): widen promoted partition tuples at manifest read

Replaces the comparison-time partition promotion with a reader-side
projection, per review.

The earlier comparison-time promotion only reached the pruning
evaluators, so a promoted partition column still mismatched in the delete
index: a data file's int partition never matched an eq delete or DV keyed
by long, dropping or mis-applying deletes. Projecting the partition tuple
fixes pruning and delete matching in one place.

* fix(scan): tighten promotion gate, borrow unpromoted bounds, guard tuple length

Addresses review feedback:
- Gate `partition_types_differ` on the type pairs `promoted_partition` actually
  widens (int->long/unknown, float->double/unknown) instead of any primitive
  difference, so a decimal-precision widening or a dropped non-numeric source no
  longer deep-clones every manifest entry on every scan.
- `InclusiveMetricsEvaluator::promote_bound` returns `Cow` and `Datum::promote_to`
  returns `Option`, so a bound that does not widen (e.g. a string or binary) is
  borrowed instead of cloned per data file during planning.
- `DataFile::promoted_partition` returns `DataInvalid` when the stored tuple and
  the spec partition type have different lengths, instead of silently dropping
  trailing values (and the partition-scoped deletes they would match).
- Drop the two delete-index unit tests that only re-exercised `promoted_partition`
  plus `Struct` equality, already covered by the data_file and scan-level tests.

* test(scan): add end-to-end promotion scan regressions for deletes

Adds plan_files scan regressions over a promoted partition column, routing an
old-schema manifest through the reader-side widening:
- A v3 deletion vector written after the promotion against the older data file.
  Without the widening the DV partition check errors (long(7) vs int(7)); the
  test guards that the data file's partition widens so the DV attaches.
- An equality delete written before the promotion against the older data file,
  so both sides widen to long. Confirms the pre-existing match is preserved.

Parameterizes the equality-delete fixture on whether the delete predates the
promotion, and adds a v3 deletion-vector fixture.

* fix(scan): copy dropped partition sources through unchanged

A dropped partition source resolves to the Unknown primitive type.
Widening its stored value to the promotion ceiling keyed on the backing
literal, so a date (stored as an int) was silently promoted to long.
The promotion gate skips a manifest whose only type difference is a
dropped source, so a data manifest that widened a dropped date diverged
from the delete manifest that left it alone, detaching the delete.

Copy dropped-source values through unchanged and restrict the gate to
genuine int to long and float to double promotions on live columns.

* fix(scan): normalize dropped numeric partition sources by written type

* Feedback

---------

Co-authored-by: Isaac <no-reply@databricks.com>

subject: fix(scan): validate deletion vector delete tasks (#3145)
body:
* docs: design delete task validation

* fix(scan): validate delete task construction

* refactor(scan): use validated delete task builder

* refactor(scan): centralize deletion vector validation

* style(scan): format validated delete task changes

* fix(scan): satisfy public API and license checks

* test(scan): adapt merged reader fixtures

* refactor(scan): encapsulate delete file metadata

* fix(scan): propagate invalid delete task errors

* fix(scan): unwrap the delete-file builder in the scan test

`FileScanTaskDeleteFile::builder().build()` returns `Result` since this
branch made it validate deletion-vector metadata, and this call site was
missed, so `cargo check --all-targets` failed with E0308 once the branch
was rebased onto a main that also compiles the lib test target.

The task built here is a complete equality delete, so validation cannot
fail; `.unwrap()` matches how the other tests in this file build tasks.

* refactor(scan): make delete-file byte offsets unsigned

Addresses @blackmwk's review. content_offset and content_size_in_bytes
are byte quantities, so Option<u64> makes a negative unrepresentable
instead of something every layer re-checks.

That collapses the three findings into one change:

- 'Why not change it to u64?' / 'Ditto': the getters and fields are u64.
- 'This duplicates a lot.': the duplication existed only to build the
  'deletion vector' vs 'delete file' prefix for two near-identical
  negative-value errors. Both are gone, and the remaining presence
  checks collapse to one lookup plus one error site.
- 'I think this should also apply to non deletion vector?': it now does,
  and unconditionally. The i64 -> u64 conversion happens once in
  TryFrom<&DeleteFileContext>, where the manifest value enters, so every
  delete-file kind is covered rather than only Puffin position deletes.

Also addresses @mbutrovich's deserialization concern from the same
review: FileScanTaskDeleteFile derives plain Deserialize, so a scan plan
rebuilt on a worker never passes through build(). With u64 fields, serde
itself rejects a negative offset, so a hand-written or corrupted plan
fails before any loader code runs -- stronger than the runtime check it
replaces.

Downstream, validate_deletion_vector_task loses its two
u64::try_from conversions; the values are already u64.

Tests: the negative cases moved from the builder to the manifest
boundary (test_delete_context_rejects_negative_*), including the non-DV
case, and the two loader tests now assert serde refuses the value.

cargo test -p iceberg --lib: 1683 passed, 0 failed.
cargo fmt --all -- --check and cargo clippy -p iceberg --all-targets
-D warnings: clean. public-api.txt updated for the two getters.

Signed-off-by: linhongyu510 <linhongyu510@gmail.com>

* refactor(scan): validate delete files on deserialize and enforce size pairing

Address review follow-ups on the delete-file validation design:

- Route FileScanTaskDeleteFile deserialization through a FileScanTaskDeleteFileSerde
  mirror that builds via builder().build(), so a deletion vector rebuilt from a
  serialized scan plan (planner->worker path) passes validate() like a manifest-
  built task. A malformed plan now fails at deserialize time instead of reaching a
  loader expect/ok_or_else.
- Enforce the spec pairing rule for every delete-file kind: content_size_in_bytes
  is required whenever content_offset is present, not only for deletion vectors.
- Replace two builder-only duplicate tests with one driving the missing-coordinate
  check through get_deletes_for_data_file, where the manifest entry is converted.
- Reword PR-history-laden comments to describe the code as it is now.

cargo test -p iceberg --lib: 1683 passed, 0 failed.

* docs(scan): clarify deletion vector loader extraction

subject: fix(spec): Skip the partition name check once the source column is dropped (#3420)
body:
* fix(spec): skip the partition name check once the source column is dropped

`validate_schema_field_names` rejected any new schema field whose name
matched a partition field name in any spec, unless some schema already
had that name. Iceberg keeps specs forever, so a name used by a spec
whose source column has since been dropped stayed reserved even though
the spec is only retained to interpret old metadata.

Iceberg Java runs the same check, in `checkAndAddPartitionName`, as
`setCurrentSchema` rebuilds every spec. It skips a field whose source
column is absent from the new schema, and otherwise allows the name only
for the source column itself:

    boolean sourceFieldExists = schema.findField(sourceColumnId) != null;
    if (sourceFieldExists) {
      Preconditions.checkArgument(
          schemaField == null || schemaField.fieldId() == sourceColumnId, ...);
    }

Adopt that rule. It keeps every spec in scope, so nothing that was
rejected before is accepted now unless its source column is gone, and it
drops the `name_exists_in_any_schema` escape hatch, which was a
Rust-only approximation of the identity-partition case.

The check now reads partition fields rather than schema names, so its
result no longer depends on whether the schema or the spec is added
first.

`partition_name_exists` loses its only caller and is removed.

Note a related divergence this does not address: `build()` rebinds the
default spec with `bind()`, which requires the source column to exist,
so dropping the source column of the *current* spec still fails. Java
uses `buildUnchecked()` there and tolerates it.

subject: fix(spec): accept partition specs produced by spec evolution (#3431)
body:
* fix(spec): accept partition specs produced by spec evolution

Partition spec evolution produces specs that the spec builders rejected:

- A source column can have more than one partition field. Adding hour(ts) to a
  spec that has day(ts) is allowed, and format version 1 tables keep each
  removed field as a `void` placeholder. Binding an unbound spec
  (`UnboundPartitionSpec::bind`, `PartitionSpecBuilder::new_from_unbound`, and
  so `TableMetadataBuilder::add_partition_spec`) and loading the legacy v1
  `partition-spec` field ran the authoring-time redundancy check and rejected
  these specs. Both now skip it, as Java does.
  `PartitionSpecBuilder::add_unbound_field` and
  `UnboundPartitionSpecBuilder::add_partition_field` still reject redundant
  fields.
- Removing identity(category) from a format version 1 spec leaves a void field
  named `category`. Both the spec builder and the table metadata builder
  allowed only identity fields to share the name of their source column. Void
  fields may now do the same, matching Java's `alwaysNull`.

Share the identity-or-void name rule through `Transform::may_share_name_with_source`
and name void in its error. Check names before redundancy in `add_unbound_field`,
document the authoring-vs-bind split, and pin it with tests, including a v2

subject: feat(transaction): let a snapshot operation report removed files and rewrite manifests (#3253)
body:
* Let a snapshot operation report the files it removed

The snapshot summary could only count what the caller asked to remove, so an
operation that skips a path it never had, or is handed the same path twice,
inflated deleted-data-files and deleted-records. SnapshotProduceOperation now
reports the entries it actually marked Deleted, each with the schema and
partition spec of the manifest that recorded it, and the summary counts those.

Two changes follow from it. The manifests are produced before the summary,
since the counts are only known once the operation has run, which means the
added data files are cloned rather than taken. And the full-table truncate that
drops the previous totals is gated on a new operation hook instead of on the
operation being Overwrite: a partial overwrite keeps the totals, and with
truncate off update_totals needs a saturating subtraction so removing more than
the previous total does not underflow.

* Keep manifest names unique across a commit

The manifest name is built inline in new_manifest_writer from the metadata
location, the commit uuid and a counter, so anything else that needs to write a
manifest for the same commit has to reinvent it, and a name invented elsewhere
is neither unique within the commit nor findable by orphan cleanup after a
failed one. Pull the name out into new_manifest_path, and make the counter an
AtomicU64 so it can be bumped behind a shared reference.

* Write a manifest under the schema and spec it was written with

new_manifest_writer hardcoded the table's current schema and default partition
spec, so an operation that rewrites an existing manifest could not keep the
schema and spec that manifest's entries were recorded under, and building a
writer by hand instead means losing the encryption manager the method already
branches on: on an encrypted table the manifest would go out in plaintext while
its key metadata said otherwise. The schema and partition spec become arguments,
and the added-files path passes the table's current ones.

* test(transaction): cover partial overwrite and per-file spec in snapshot summary

Co-authored-by: Marco Kroll <216147982+mkroll-db@users.noreply.github.com>

* Drop the full-table truncation from the snapshot summary

Java and PyIceberg derive totals from the files an operation marks deleted, with no truncation path.

* Omit a summary total that would go negative, as Java does

* Name the removed-file fields and take the manifest spec by ref

* Take the added files again instead of cloning them for the summary

* Assert an operation reports exactly the files it marked deleted

* Say in the removed_data_files doc what it must match

* Summarize deleted files from the producer's list, as pyiceberg does

Drops the removed_data_files hook and the manifest-first reorder, and truncation defaults back to every overwrite.

* Check that deletion summaries match manifest entries

* Format dropped-source integer partition values

subject: fix(spec): reuse the highest matching partition field id, not an arbitrary one (#3413)
body:
* fix(spec): reuse the highest matching partition field id, not an arbitrary one

`reuse_partition_field_ids` collects (source_id, transform) -> field_id
into a HashMap with no merge function, so when several specs give one
pair different field ids the last one visited wins. `partition_specs` is
itself a HashMap, so the winner changes from run to run and the same
input metadata yields different output.

Keep the highest id of each pair, as Iceberg Java does:

    Collectors.toMap(
        field -> Pair.of(field.sourceId(), field.transform().toString()),
        PartitionField::fieldId,
        Math::max)

Divergent ids for one pair cannot be produced by this crate, since the
reuse rule keeps them converged, but they can be read from tables
written before the rule existed or by writers that do not apply it.

* comments

* Deterministic test

subject: fix(reader): rewrite NOT out of the read predicate before pruning (#3416)
body:
* fix(reader): rewrite NOT out of the read predicate before pruning

The reader fans a FileScanTask's predicate to the row-group metrics
evaluator and the page-index evaluator, both conservative (inclusive)
filters that cannot soundly negate a NOT node. The row-group evaluator's
naive `!inner` flips a MIGHT_MATCH bound to CANT_MATCH. For NOT(x > 5) over
a row group spanning [0, 10] that prunes a group which does contain matching
rows (silent data loss). The page-index evaluator rejects NOT outright,
aborting the read. A FileScanTask built or deserialized outside TableScan
carries an un-normalized predicate, so a raw NOT reaches both.

Rewrite NOT out of the predicate once, where it is first bound in the read
pipeline, so every consumer sees a NOT-free predicate.

* PR feedback

subject: fix(arrow): reconcile evolved nested structs by field id, not position (#3255)
body:
* fix(arrow): reconcile evolved nested structs by field id, not position

When a struct gains a field (schema evolution) after a data file was written,
the file's struct has fewer children than the table schema. RecordBatchTransformer
promoted such columns with arrow_cast::cast, which matches struct/list/map children
positionally -- so every child after the gap shifts and types collide, e.g.
'Casting from Utf8 to Struct' when a scalar lands on an added list<struct>.

Replace the flat cast with a PromotePlan that is resolved once per file when
the BatchTransform is built: nested struct children are matched to the target
schema by PARQUET:field_id, recursing through list/large-list/map, so the
per-batch work is just index lookups and array assembly. Absent optional
children are filled with typed nulls; absent required children error, as do
absent children with an initial-default (not yet wired up for nested fields)
and source structs whose children carry no field ids, rather than silently
producing wrong data. Primitives still use cast for valid Iceberg promotions.
Mirrors iceberg-java's by-field-id nested readers.

Closes #2617

* test(arrow): cover appended nested struct field on promote

Add a unit test for struct<a, b> -> struct<a, b, c>, the append case of
nested schema evolution. The existing middle-insert test already covers
by-id matching; this pins the "expected 3 got 2" failure mode.

* fix(arrow): reconcile nested reorder and rename by field id

Always build a PromotePlan for a present column and pass through only
when that plan is a no-op. equals_datatype ignored nested names and
field ids, so a reorder or same-type rename kept the file layout.

Id-less nested children still match by position when their types line
up, which covers maps. Nested initial-default stays unsupported (#3261).

* fix(arrow): error when only some nested fields have ids

The positional fallback stays for a fully id-less struct. If some
children have field ids and some do not, null-filling the rest would
drop data, so that now errors. A same-type id-less reorder is still
positional; it cannot be detected without ids.

* fix(arrow): cast id-less nested fields by position

Name mapping only stamps top-level ids. When the child counts match,
pair by position and let build check each child, so an int still
promotes to long. A different count, or ids on only some children,
still errors.

* test(arrow): compare remaining promote results as whole arrays

Use invalid_data! for the PromotePlan DataInvalid errors, matching main.

* fix(arrow): accept either list offset width from the file

A Parquet Arrow schema hint can make a list column LargeList while the
table schema is List. Main cast that column; PromotePlan rejected it.

* fix(arrow): apply nested identity constants and drop LargeList targets

A missing nested field that is an identity partition source takes that
partition value before initial-default or null. schema_to_arrow_schema
always emits List, so a LargeList target now errors instead of building
a plan; a LargeList file column still promotes to List.

The remaining promote tests compare whole arrays. Error tests check
ErrorKind, including field ids on only some children.

* Simplify PromotePlan and dedup nested promotion tests

* fix(arrow): address final review on nested field-id promotion

- Add a reader-level test that writes an old nested schema to Parquet and
  reads it back through an evolved one, pinning that parquet-rs attaches
  field ids to struct children, list elements, and map keys and values
- Reject duplicate source field ids and nested sources read as a
  non-nested type when the plan is built
- Report non-struct map entries as DataInvalid
- Pin the id-less same-type reorder fallback with a test until #1845
- Assert map data types, since map array equality skips field names
- Point at #3378 where the projection mask skips all-missing structs

* test(arrow): cover sliced list promotion with a null slot

subject: feat(reader): page-index pruning for FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY decimals (#3328)
body:
Decimals with precision > 18 are stored as FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY, which the
page-index evaluator skipped, so inequality and IN predicates on them got no
page pruning (over-selection only, never dropped rows). Decode those bounds
with i128_from_be_bytes, matching the row-group statistics path.

Guard against truncated ColumnIndex bounds: a bound whose width differs from
the column's declared type_length signals a column_index_truncate_length
truncation, and a truncated byte prefix no longer preserves the two's
complement numeric ordering of decimals. Reject it so the column skips pruning
rather than decode the wrong number. parquet-rs never truncates decimal column
indexes, so this only defends against files written by other implementations.

Benchmark

A throwaway benchmark on a 1,000,000-row single-column decimal(30,2) file
(precision > 18 -> FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY), 100 pages in one row group, read
fully in memory so timing is decode-only. A `col > threshold` predicate sweeps
selectivity. "read full file" is today's behavior (FLBA decimals skip page
pruning); "read ms" applies the page-index RowSelection this change produces.

    1,000,000 rows in 100 pages, 1 row group
    read full file : 3.431 ms

      predicate (keep) | rows read | eval us | read ms | speedup
                   1%  |    10,000 |    17.5 |   0.038 |   90.0x
                  10%  |   100,000 |    17.1 |   0.330 |   10.4x
                  50%  |   500,000 |    16.6 |   1.629 |    2.1x
                 100%  | 1,000,000 |    16.3 |   3.397 |    1.0x

The win tracks predicate selectivity; eval() adds a constant ~17 us per row
group per scan, negligible against the millisecond read. The benefit only
materializes where page-index row selection runs: MoR tables or
with_row_selection_enabled(true). Reproducer in the PR description.

Follow-up to #3314.

subject: fix(arrow): decode short BYTE_ARRAY decimal row-group stats (#3364)
body:
get_parquet_stat_min_as_datum / get_parquet_stat_max_as_datum decoded
BYTE_ARRAY decimal bounds with a strict 16-byte conversion. Parquet
stores these as minimal-length big-endian two's-complement values, so
any bound shorter than 16 bytes failed to convert and aborted the
row-group read.

Use the variable-length, sign-extending i128_from_be_bytes helper, as
the FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY arm already does. Bounds longer than 16 bytes
still return DataInvalid. Empty bounds also return DataInvalid instead
of decoding as zero, which could otherwise prune matching row groups.

Closes #3280

subject: perf(arrow): build the delete row selection from deleted ranges (#3454)
body:
* perf(arrow): build the delete row selection from deleted ranges

build_deletes_row_selection walked the delete vector one position at a time, so
a run of deleted rows cost one iteration per row. It now reads the deleted
positions as ranges, which makes a run one step. Short runs are still walked
with `next`, because roaring's `next_range` binary-searches the rest of an array
container on every call and is slower than `next` for single positions.

Row groups that are not selected are skipped with `skip_to` instead of walking
their deletes. The new range iterator is crate-private; the public
`DeleteVector::iter` and `DeleteVectorIterator::advance_to` are unchanged.

* Address review: fix advance_to (#3400), randomized reader test

- DeleteVectorIterator::advance_to now handles a target in a missing later
  bitmap, a target below the current bitmap, and a call before the first next
  (the cases in #3400), with the same three-way check as skip_to. Dropped the
  stale comments about roaring-rs#314 and the git dependency.
- Randomized test for build_deletes_row_selection: random row group layouts
  and selections over mixed_delete_vectors, against a selection built one
  deleted position at a time.
- full_range no longer overflows at u64::MAX.
- One Buffered enum instead of pending/pending_range.
- Model tests also skip backwards, mixed_delete_vectors has gaps between
  bitmaps, a model test for advance_to, the #3400 cases split per test, and
  doc updates for ranges, skip_to and RUN_PROBE_LEN.

* Address review: deletes past the file end, runs across 2^16, ranges() docs
